Falsifiability.question: The _____ was Property of a statement that can be logically contradicted.
Falsifiability.fact: Falsifiability is a standard of evaluation of scientific statements, including theories and hypotheses. Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages
Falsifiability.question: It was introduced by the philosopher of science Karl Popper in his book The Logic of Scientific Discovery (_____)
Falsifiability.fact: It was introduced by the philosopher of science Karl Popper in his book The Logic of Scientific Discovery (1934).

Falsifiability.subject: Indian Languages

Falsifiability.fact: Popper claimed that induction is not needed in science, that is, he rejected that we learn by the repetition of observations and considered that logical induction was a fallacy. This led Popper's student and collaborator David Miller to write "the mission is to classify truths, not to certify them".

Popper accepted Hume's argument and therefore viewed progress in science as the result of quasi-induction, which is induction without inference rules and which he also called the "path of science".

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Most of Fes el-Jdid's outer perimeter was protected by a set of double walls; a tall inner wall with heavy square towers at regular intervals and a smaller outer wall with minor towers.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Today, an original section of these walls has been well-preserved between the _____ and Agdal Gardens, inside the perimeter of the Dar al-Makhzen
Fortifications of Fez.fact: Today, an original section of these walls has been well-preserved between the Lalla Mina and Agdal Gardens, inside the perimeter of the Dar al-Makhzen.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: The heyday of the _____ thus translated also into a golden age for Fes as well
Fortifications of Fez.fact: Nonetheless, the Marinids did also restore and repair the walls of Fes el-Bali, in addition to devoting their attention to the construction of prestigious madrasas and other embellishments in the old city. The heyday of the Marinids thus translated also into a golden age for Fes as well.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Today, Fes el-Jdid's walls and gates still date to a large extent from the Marinid period, generally from _____'qub's initial construction
Fortifications of Fez.fact: Today, Fes el-Jdid's walls and gates still date to a large extent from the Marinid period, generally from Abu Yusuf Ya'qub's initial construction.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: However, some sections have been expanded over the years, with those of the Dar al-_____, in particular, being extended multiple times to accommodate new gardens and extensions of the palace
Fortifications of Fez.fact: However, some sections have been expanded over the years, with those of the Dar al-Makhzen, in particular, being extended multiple times to accommodate new gardens and extensions of the palace.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: The Saadi sultan Muhammad ash-Sheikh besieged and conquered Fes in _____, after strong resistance
Fortifications of Fez.fact: The Saadi sultan Muhammad ash-Sheikh besieged and conquered Fes in 1549, after strong resistance.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: In _____-55 a surviving member of the Wattasid dynasty reestablished control over Fes and the Saadis were forced to once again besiege and reconquer Fes right away
Fortifications of Fez.fact: In 1554-55 a surviving member of the Wattasid dynasty reestablished control over Fes and the Saadis were forced to once again besiege and reconquer Fes right away.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Upon retaking the city, the _____ authorities took revenge upon some of the local leaders and treated the general population poorly, further enshrining the inhabitants' hostility to the new dynasty
Fortifications of Fez.fact: The Saadi sultan Muhammad ash-Sheikh besieged and conquered Fes in 1549, after strong resistance. In 1554-55 a surviving member of the Wattasid dynasty reestablished control over Fes and the Saadis were forced to once again besiege and reconquer Fes right away.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Presumably as a result of this persisting tension, the _____ built a number of new forts and bastions around the city which appear to be aimed at keeping control over the local population
Fortifications of Fez.fact: In 1554-55 a surviving member of the Wattasid dynasty reestablished control over Fes and the Saadis were forced to once again besiege and reconquer Fes right away. Presumably as a result of this persisting tension, the Saadis built a number of new forts and bastions around the city which appear to be aimed at keeping control over the local population.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: They were mostly located on higher ground overlooking Fes el-_____, from which they would have been easily able to bombard the city with canons
Fortifications of Fez.fact: They were mostly located on higher ground overlooking Fes el-Bali, from which they would have been easily able to bombard the city with canons. These include the Kasbah Tamdert, just inside the city walls near Bab Ftouh, and the forts of Borj Nord (Borj al-Shamali) on the hills to the north, Borj Sud (Borj al-Janoub) on the hills to the south, and the Borj Sheikh Ahmed to the west, at a point in Fes el-Jdid's walls that was closest to Fes el-Bali.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Two other bastions, _____ and Borj Sidi Bou Nafa', were also built along Fes el-Jdid's walls south of Borj Sheikh Ahmed
Fortifications of Fez.fact: Two other bastions, Borj Twil and Borj Sidi Bou Nafa', were also built along Fes el-Jdid's walls south of Borj Sheikh Ahmed.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Some of them may have been built with the help of Christian European prisoners of war from the Saadis' victory over Portuguese at the Battle of the Three Kings in _____
Fortifications of Fez.fact: Some of them may have been built with the help of Christian European prisoners of war from the Saadis' victory over Portuguese at the Battle of the Three Kings in 1578.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages

Fortifications of Fez.fact: He built the Kasbah Cherarda (also called the Kasbah al-Khemis) to the north of Fes el-Jdid and of the Royal Palace in order to house a large part of his tribal troops.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: The '_____ continued to rebuild or restore various monuments, as well as to expand the grounds of the Royal Palace a number of times
Fortifications of Fez.fact: The 'Alawis continued to rebuild or restore various monuments, as well as to expand the grounds of the Royal Palace a number of times.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: The final and most significant change to Fes's topography was made during the reign of Moulay Hasan I (_____-1894), who finally connected Fes el-Jdid and Fes el-Bali by building a walled corridor betw
Fortifications of Fez.fact: The final and most significant change to Fes's topography was made during the reign of Moulay Hasan I (1873-1894), who finally connected Fes el-Jdid and Fes el-Bali by building a walled corridor between them.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: Within this new corridor, between the two cities, lay new gardens and summer palaces used by the royals and the capital's high society, such as the _____
Fortifications of Fez.fact: Within this new corridor, between the two cities, lay new gardens and summer palaces used by the royals and the capital's high society, such as the Jnan Sbil Gardens.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: The outline of Fes el-Jdid (and of the _____ inside it) was also altered many times in this period
Fortifications of Fez.fact: The 'Alawis continued to rebuild or restore various monuments, as well as to expand the grounds of the Royal Palace a number of times. The outline of Fes el-Jdid (and of the Royal Palace inside it) was also altered many times in this period.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: The term borj (_____: برج), generally meaning "tower", was applied to a number of heavily fortified military structures and bastions, especially those of the Saadi era
Fortifications of Fez.fact: The term "kasbah" (Arabic: قَـصَـبَـة, romanized: qaṣabah) was used to denote a large number of fortified enclosures ranging from small garrison forts to larger citadels, many of them named after the ethnic or geographic origin of the soldiers posted there. The term borj (Arabic: برج), generally meaning "tower", was applied to a number of heavily fortified military structures and bastions, especially those of the Saadi era.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages
Fortifications of Fez.question: It was once the citadel of the _____ and then the Almohad authorities, and continued to be used as the governor's residence even up to the 20th century
Fortifications of Fez.fact: It was once the citadel of the Almoravids and then the Almohad authorities, and continued to be used as the governor's residence even up to the 20th century.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Kasbah an-Nouar: Also called Kasbah Filala, it dates from the Almohad and 'Alawi periods.

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Kasbah Tamdert: Near Bab Ftouh gate in the southeast, it dates from the Saadi period.

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Borj Nord: This Saadi fort bears the clearest signs of European influence in its structure, and stands on the hills north of the city, near the Marinid Tombs.

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Borj Sud: The "sister" of Borj Nord, it stands on the hills overlooking Fes el-Bali from the south. Borj Sheikh Ahmed: The northernmost and easternmost bastion, this one was built at the corner of the walls closest to Fes el-Bali.

Fortifications of Fez.subject: Indian Languages

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Today it can also be prominently seen overlooking the southern edge of the Jnan Sbil Gardens.

Fortifications of Fez.fact: It exists alongside the Bab Mahrouk Cemetery and Kasbah an-Nouar.

Fortifications of Fez.fact: Bab Bou Jeloud: The main western entrance to Fes el-Bali today (located further east than Bab Mahrouk), and an iconic monument of the medina of Fez. Bab Ftouh: The main southwestern gate of Fes el-Bali.

Fortifications of Fez.fact: It dates essentially from the Almohad period (12th-13th century) in its current form. Bab Guissa: The main northeastern gate of Fes el-Bali, also dating in its current form from the Almohad period (12th-13th century).
